title: Onboarding exception flow and compatibility annotations for untrusted model variants
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Clarify requirements for admitting new open-source model variants that fail strict runtime compatibility checks, define an exception workflow (temporary admission with constraints), and specify a machine-readable compatibility annotation schema to drive runtime routing and pin decisions.
background: We routinely ingest community-submitted model weights. Some variants are functionally useful but do not meet the full binary/runtime checks required for automatic unpinned admission (mismatched KV cache layout, unsupported attention kernel patterns, or nonstandard tokenizer metadata). Current intake is binary: either 'admit and pin' or 'reject', which blocks useful variants and drives ad-hoc manual processes. Engineering and runtime teams proposed a controlled exception flow to allow time-limited admission with metadata annotations to limit traffic and enforce safe fallbacks.
scope_in_scope: Define exception admission criteria and required mitigation fields (time-to-triage TTL, canary percent, fallback variant mapping)
Design a compact compatibility annotation schema (compat_level, kernel_hints, tokenizer_hash, recommended_pin) consumed by runtime and console
Implement acceptance criteria and lightweight QA checklist for exception admissions
Console UI: surface exception flags and automated warnings on catalog entries
API: allow partner teams to request exception admission and attach justification + test artifacts
scope_out_of_scope: Full automation of runtime kernel generation for unsupported models
Large-scale re-architecting of serving runtime to accept all formats
Billing or pricing changes for exception variants
requirements: R1: Exception admission must be recorded with a TTL (default 21 days) after which the variant is suspended unless extended by a maintainer
R2: Catalog entries in exception state must include: justification text, minimal test artifacts (inference sample, eval metrics), and at least one recommended fallback variant key

R3: The compatibility annotation schema must be a flat JSON-LD compatible payload no larger than 2 KB and include keys: compat_level (enum), tokenizer_hash, kernel_hints (list), recommended_pin (model key or empty), safety_flags (list)
R4: Runtime must route up to X% of traffic to exception variants as canary (configurable, default 2%) with automatic failover to recommended_pin on error or latency regression
R5: Console must show exception state prominently, with a one-click suspend/extend button for catalog owners
R6: Intake API must validate presence of required fields and reject submissions missing justification or test artifacts
R7: Security review must be run for exception admissions that opt into dedicated capacity deployments
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Submitter can create an exception admission via API or Console with required fields and TTL; ticket recorded in catalog audit log
AC2: Runtime honors compat annotations by tagging request traces with compat_level and kernel_hints, visible in tracing UI
AC3: Canary traffic percentage enforces default and obeys per-variant overrides; when runtime observes >=2x error rate vs fallback, it automatically routes new requests to fallback
AC4: Console displays exception metadata and allows owner to extend TTL; extension and suspension are recorded in audit logs
AC5: Automated unit/integration tests for API validation and runtime failover exist and pass in CI
AC6: Security team confirms review path and sign-off checkbox is present in exception admission flow for dedicated/private deployments
proposed_solution: Introduce a three-part flow: (1) Intake API + Console form for 'exception admission' capturing justification, test artifacts, and the compact compatibility annotation; (2) Catalog metadata model updated with exception state, TTL, owner, and recommended_fallback; (3) Runtime and Console changes to honor compat annotations for routing and observability. Default canary percent is 2% with automatic rollback rules. Provide a light-weight 'extend' endpoint for owners and generate a start-of-life issue assigned to runtime team for prioritized remediation.
tradeoffs: Allowing exceptions increases operational surface area and may temporarily expose users to degraded variants; mitigated by low default canary and automatic failover
Requiring test artifacts increases intake friction for submitters but reduces downstream toil and runtime incidents
Keeping schema compact reduces telemetry richness but enforces predictable runtime parsing and storage costs
migration_plan: 1) Schema bump in catalog service to accept compat annotations (backwards compatible)
2) Launch API + Console 'request exception' alpha behind feature flag for internal teams
3) Enable runtime canary routing for feature-flagged variants and validate automatic failover through synthetic tests
4) Roll out to external submitters after 2-week internal alpha and documented runbook
5) After 3 months, measure remediation completion rate; if <60% extend TTL policy and escalate to catalog maintainers
tests: Unit: API schema validation tests for missing fields and malformed annotation payloads
Integration: end-to-end canary routing with simulated errors to verify failover to recommended_pin
E2E: Console flow that creates exception admission, shows metadata, extends TTL, and records audit entries
Load: ensure compat annotation parsing adds <1% overhead to catalog read latency at 1000 RPS
metrics: Metric 1: Number of exception admissions per week
Metric 2: Median time from exception admission to remediation (pin or runtime support)
Metric 3: Canary error-rate vs fallback error-rate and automatic rollback frequency
Metric 4: % of exception admissions with complete test artifacts on first submission
Metric 5: Catalog read latency delta after schema change
